contribution.position: Holding my earlier reliability position, with one new point. QA (axis:risk) says peak_cpu is 55%, comfortably inside the 70% budget. That conflicts with artifact:perf-report, which records peak_cpu at 93% at peak load against the 70% budget. Nothing in the artifact list shows a 55% figure, so I treat that number as unsupported. It may come from a different run, load level, or build, but the transcript does not say. If 93% is correct, the headroom QA calls comfortable does not exist, and the retry-storm exposure in artifact:incident-log (two sev2 incidents last quarter) stays open. Ops (axis:operability) cites artifact:ops-runbook for deploy and rollback steps. Per the artifact text, runbook v4 covers deploy and rollback only. It does not show retry caps, backoff limits, or a response to a retry storm, so it does not address the failure mode in the incident log. artifact:test-report (412 passed, 0 failed, 87% coverage) shows functional correctness, but no artifact shows retry or backoff behavior exercised under peak load. Product's cost point (artifact:cost-sheet, +3% against a 5% ceiling) is a separate axis and does not bear on reliability. It also does not appear to include any cost of fixing CPU headroom. Missing evidence: (1) the source and conditions of the 55% figure, reconciled with the 93% measurement; (2) a peak-load test showing retries stay bounded; (3) confirmation that the root causes of last quarter's retry storms are fixed or capped.
